A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GameArena research work and complete Appendices A–E. Pages 2–32 have identical extracted text and rendered pixels. First-page differences concern authorship, affiliations, footnotes and version metadata; the scientific text is unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five LLMs using 2240 gameplay sessions and a 100-participant user study, with outcomes in Section 4, Tables 2–3 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v4 retains the original gameplay evaluations, 100-participant user-study results, controlled comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The game procedures, retrospective reasoning analysis and DSPy prompt optimization are identical in Sections 2–4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Akinator, Taboo and Bluffing using the same gameplay data, human study and comparison scenarios. Appendix B retains the same game-secret sets.

E2.justification: The same five LLMs are evaluated. Chatbot Arena remains the user-experience and data-efficiency comparator, and Table 4 and Appendix C retain identical benchmark comparator sets.

E3.justification: Model configurations, prompt optimization, metrics and sampling are unchanged. Both report 2240 gameplay sessions, 100 study participants and two 50-session subsets per game in the consistency experiment (Section 4; Appendix B).

E4.justification: Figure 5 and Appendix B retain the same consistency analysis across diverse game-secret subsets. Appendix E retains all five case studies, including the Taboo failure examples.

E5.justification: Table 2 and Figure 5 retain standard deviations across five system prompts. Appendix D retains the same Kendall's tau tests, RBO permutation procedure using 1000 random rankings and significance reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings are identical throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Claude 3.5 Sonnet's Akinator win rate remains 0.55±0.11 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The formal game formulation in Section 2.2, metric definitions and equations in Sections 3.2 and 4.5, and statistical derivations in Appendix D are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic gameplay evaluation, specific reasoning capabilities, step-by-step reasoning data and user engagement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model behavior and benchmark-ranking differences are unchanged. The limitations of Taboo outcome scores, including wins without identifying the secret word, remain documented in Table 4 and Appendix E.

D1.justification: The DSPy setup, game rules, gameplay and retrospective-analysis prompts, curated game secrets and statement promising release of gaming data are unchanged. No technical or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the reference list are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to static benchmarks, Chatbot Arena, other game evaluations and RedTeam Arena.

P1.justification: v4 adds Ion Stoica, marks Anze Xie as an equal contributor, adds Berkeley and Snowflake affiliations, and adds an internship acknowledgment. Version metadata and correspondence punctuation also change; scientific prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: First-page typesetting changes accommodate the longer author and affiliation lines, affiliation superscripts and expanded footnote. All figures, tables and layouts on pages 2–32 remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 updates attribution and affiliations but preserves the methods, empirical evidence, statistical analyses, reproducibility information and scientific exposition, including every appendix. The limited front-matter changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
